# An ordering proof written against the log proves nothing

**Domains:** tooling, invariants

**Tags:** invariant-backing, coverage-gate

**Related ADRs:** ADR-0175

A claim that names an ordering, such as "the final lock replacement is the commit point", is
not proven by asserting the order of the operation lines a transaction prints. The line is
emitted at a fixed call site, so moving the write it describes leaves the printed order
untouched: ADR-0175's journal survived a mutation applying the lock before every resident
quarantine while both an ordered-log assertion and the whole package stayed green
(2026-07-29). The rollback path hid it as well, because `restorePriors` walks in reverse and
so restored the early lock before halting on the ambiguous resident, leaving the collision
test's own assertions true. Prove an ordering against the observable it constrains rather
than a narration of it: pass a writer that reads the real state at each emitted step and
require that state to hold its prior value until the step that is allowed to change it.
Then mutate the production order and watch the new test go red. A proof for a timing or
ordering clause is not finished until you have seen it fail; this one was proposed during
review, built as proposed, and only mutation revealed it was inert.
